label: prop:crossing-energy-pair-cancellation
title: Mirror pairing cancels the symmetric channel
html:
Proposition. Mirror pairing cancels the symmetric channel

Proposition. Let \mathfrak{H} be a knot composite carrying p positive and m negative crossings, and let \mathfrak{H}^{\sigma} be its mirror. Then

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}) +
  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}^{\sigma})
  = 2E_{\mathrm{asym}}(\mathfrak{H})
  = 2(p + m)\sinh\lambda,

where \lambda = \ln q. The symmetric channel cancels identically and the surviving energy is purely antisymmetric.

Proof. By the decomposition, \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}) = (p - m)\cosh\lambda + (p + m)\sinh\lambda. The mirror exchanges p and m, so \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}^{\sigma}) = (m - p)\cosh\lambda + (m + p)\sinh\lambda. Adding, the \cosh terms cancel and the \sinh terms double. \square

Structural content. The cancellation is a consequence of the multiplicity mismatch between the two channels. The \cosh weight of a crossing carries the crossing sign and therefore enters the total with multiplicity p - m; the \sinh weight is blind to the crossing sign and enters with multiplicity p + m. Only a sign-blind channel can survive mirror pairing, and the antisymmetric channel is the sign-blind one.

The residue is strictly positive for q > 1 and any composite with at least one crossing, so a composite and its mirror never annihilate to zero crossing energy. The pair creation remark reads this residue as the Coulomb energy that separates a created particle-antiparticle pair.
